result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-020 (registration for an open event, atomic capacity enforcement, qr_token issuance) at commit 5044b7f, branch feature/WF02-REQ-020. Did not trust TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report or the extensive prior REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER concurrency work as a substitute for my own re-derivation. 1. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-020.md in full against all 7 acceptance criteria (§11's AC-to-design-element map) plus the additional AC4/AC5/AC6/AC7/AC8/AC9/AC-card/AC-schema/AC-catalog cases the test spec actually verifies. Every AC maps to a concrete, non-deferred design element; no 'TBD' language; open questions (§9) are stated explicitly, not silently resolved. 2. Re-ran npm run lint myself: 0 errors, 2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx:11, Nav.tsx:10 -- unrelated to this diff, both files untouched by it). Re-ran npm run build myself: apps/web (next build, Turbopack) compiled successfully; apps/bot (tsc -p tsconfig.json) clean, zero errors. Both match TEST-RUNNER's report. 3. Ran npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism myself from repo root with no DB running: 15 files / 157 passed + 15 skipped (172 total) -- the 15 skips are the DB-backed suite's own graceful self-skip (registration.db.test.ts's beforeAll probe finds no reachable Postgres, per the same ISS-0013/0014-documented discipline start.test.ts already established). Stood up my own scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432), ran `npx drizzle-kit migrate` myself (applied cleanly, zero new migration files -- confirms AC-schema's 'no schema change' claim structurally, not just via git diff --stat), then re-ran the identical vitest command: 15 files / 172 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- confirms the authoritative count TEST-RUNNER's report and test-reports/report-2026-09-07-WF02-REQ-020.yaml both state, with my own fresh execution rather than trusting the transcription (ISS-0016 from the REQ-019 run was exactly this class of trust failure -- checked for it here and found none). 4. Independent concurrency verification, a genuinely different configuration than any of the four prior runs (BACKEND-DEV: capacity=1/2-callers/20-iterations; REVIEWER: capacity=2/5-callers/50+iterations plus a raw-lock proof; TEST-RUNNER: capacity=3/4-callers/30-iterations live-dispatch): I ran capacity=1 with 10 concurrent callers (maximally-contended single-seat race), 15 iterations, calling registerForEvent directly against my own fresh fixtures each iteration (150 total concurrent registerForEvent invocations). Result: {iterations: 15, callersPerIteration: 10, capacity: 1, admittedTotal: 15, waitlistedTotal: 135, anyError: false, badIterations: [], allPassed: true} -- every single iteration produced exactly 1 admitted + 9 waitlisted, confirmed both from the returned outcomes AND a direct DB re-count of admission='admitted' rows per iteration (never more than 1), AND a per-iteration check that exactly one qr_token was issued and it was a well-formed 64-hex-char string. Fifth independent data point, zero races, adds a materially different contention shape (10-way, not 2/4/5-way) at the tightest possible capacity. 5. Independent AC3 (qr_token CSPRNG) re-verification: my own grep of apps/bot/src confirmed generateQrToken (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts:82-84) is the sole call site of both randomBytes and any token-generation logic; `git grep -n Math.random apps/bot/src` returns only a comment line (registration.ts:79) documenting the constraint, never an actual call. My own independent collision sample (20,000 tokens, generated via node:crypto's randomBytes(32).toString('hex') outside any test harness, a different sample size than TEST-RUNNER's 5,000): {N: 20000, uniqueCount: 20000, collisions: 0, badFormat: 0} -- every token matched /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/, zero collisions. 6. Independent AC7 (audit row on both admitted and waitlisted) re-verification: built my own fixtures (fresh chapter/venue/organizer/two users, capacity=1, distinct ids from any prior run) and called registerForEvent directly for two users. Read back via a direct SQL join (audit_log JOIN registrations JOIN events JOIN chapters): exactly 2 audit_log rows for entity='registration', row 1 action=registration.admit / admission=admitted / qr_token a well-formed 64-hex-char string / actor_user_id = the admitted user's own id; row 2 action=registration.waitlist / admission=waitlisted / qr_token NULL / actor_user_id = the waitlisted user's own id. Confirms both the AC7 literal requirement and the broader S8 reading §6 of the design document argues for. 7. Confirmed full requirement scope: git status --porcelain clean throughout (verified before and after all scratch work; all scratch files -- scratch-verify-req020-rv.ts, scratch-verify-req020-ac7.ts -- and the scratch docker-compose stack were deleted/torn down before this handoff). All 7 design-doc-listed files present (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts modified, apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts modified for the card wiring, apps/bot/src/i18n/types.ts, ru.ts, en.ts, apps/bot/src/index.ts modified). Grepped registration.ts/handlers/registration.ts/handlers/start.ts/index.ts for TODO/FIXME/XXX: zero matches. i18n/types.ts's registration block has exactly the 15 spec-named keys; grep for 'cardCta' across apps/bot/src returns only a comment noting its removal (event.ts:849), never a live reference -- the dead key removal (design §7.3) genuinely happened. REGISTER_CALLBACK_PATTERN is wired exactly once in index.ts, reachable. 8. docs/agents/requirements.yaml's REQ-020 entry: description and acceptance_criteria match the implemented scope precisely (open-event admit/waitlist branching, current-status-on-repeat, closed/cancelled/finished refusal with onward path, source resolution, requires_invite/requires_approval refusal, audit logging). status is still 'pending', which is correct and expected at this step -- DOC-UPDATER (Step 6) has not run yet, not staleness. 9. Judgment on the 5 filed issues (ISS-0013 through ISS-0017), none blocking this release: - ISS-0013 (CI has no Postgres service, MAJOR, from REQ-019): confirmed still open, still correctly scoped as forward-looking test-infrastructure debt, not a defect in REQ-020's own shipped correctness. Every verification in this run (mine included) executed real code against a real, locally-provisioned Postgres with real reported output -- nothing was skipped or asserted without evidence. Not blocking, for the same reasoning the REQ-019 release validation already recorded. - ISS-0014 (DB-backed vitest files race under default per-file parallelism, MINOR, from REQ-019): not applicable to my own re-runs since I always used --no-file-parallelism per the standing instruction; does not affect REQ-020's correctness. Not blocking. - ISS-0015 (REQ-019 test-spec wording inconsistency, MINOR): scoped to REQ-019's own spec file, not REQ-020. Not applicable to this release at all. - ISS-0016 (TEST-RUNNER inflated test count on REQ-019, MINOR): scoped to REQ-019's own report; REQ-020's TEST-RUNNER report and my own independent re-run both agree on 172, no discrepancy here. Not applicable/not blocking. - ISS-0017 (REQ-020 test-spec has two minor fixture defects -- missing 'e_' deep-link prefix, invalid UUID literal, MINOR): confirmed accurate by reading the affected lines of docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-020.md directly. Both defects are in the test-spec fixture text only, not in shipped apps/bot/ code; TEST-RUNNER correctly worked around both in its harness and re-verified against the real deep-link path (I independently re-exercised the real deep-link/card path via my own AC1-style direct registerForEvent calls plus a live grep-confirmed handler wiring, so the underlying registration/card behavior these two cases exist to test is independently confirmed correct regardless of the spec typos). Non-blocking; correctly left for TEST-DESIGNER to fix at the source in a future pass, per core-directives' fix-at-source discipline. Overall: this is the most correctness-critical requirement in the project to date, and every independent check I ran -- lint, build, full test suite from a cold DB, a fifth and structurally different concurrency configuration, an independent CSPRNG sample, and independent audit-log fixtures -- agrees with the prior four gates. No half-implemented scope, no stray TODOs, clean git tree.
